Despite contrary headlines, General Motors (GM) has not changed its stance on CarPlay and Android Auto support. The automaker will not be adding back support to any vehicles that have already had phone projection features removed. Here's the real story.

No, GM Has Not Reversed Its Decision to Drop CarPlay

The confusion began last week when GM announced a new software experience for its Chevrolet Silverado and GMC Sierra trucks. The company is pushing a new picture-in-picture phone mirroring system that can run CarPlay and Android Auto alongside GM's own native infotainment system.

Some outlets interpreted this news as GM backing down from its plan to abandon CarPlay, a plan first announced in 2023. Unfortunately, that's not the case. GM's original announcement was about dropping CarPlay support from its future electric vehicles, and it has been sticking to that plan, with the Cadillac Lyriq EV being the only exception.

GM has never removed CarPlay or Android Auto from any of its gas-powered vehicles. So the addition of phone projection to the Chevrolet Silverado and GMC Sierra trucks does not mean the automaker has caved under pressure and is bringing CarPlay back to its EVs.

A GM spokesperson confirmed this to Joanna Stern, who posted the following on X today:

The confusion is understandable. GM CEO Mary Barra previously said in an interview that the automaker would eventually drop CarPlay and Android Auto from its gas-powered vehicles too. However, the company quickly clarified that gas vehicles would continue to offer phone projection 'for the foreseeable future.'

Long story short, nothing has changed. GM is not bringing CarPlay back to its electric vehicles. There is no change in strategy. Maybe we should see GM offering a picture-in-picture solution for some gas vehicles as a sign that it realizes its decision to drop CarPlay is unpopular. But I think that's too generous a read.

Also worth noting: John Gruber's headline on this story is the best.
